title: Opening counsels for a consecrated virgin
english: Love the Lord, and he will love you; serve him, and he will give light to your heart.
Honor your mother as the mother of Christ, and do not provoke the grey hair of the one who bore you.
Love your sisters as daughters of your mother, and do not abandon the way of peace.
When the sun rises, let it see the book in your hands, and after the second hour, your work.
Pray without ceasing, and remember Christ, who gave you birth.
Avoid meetings with men, so that idols do not arise in your soul and become a stumbling block for you at the time of prayer.
You have Christ as your beloved; cast away from yourself all men, and you will not live a shameful life.
Put anger and wrath far from you, and do not let bearing of malice lodge within you.
Do not say, "Today I will eat and tomorrow I will not eat," because you are not doing this with understanding. For it will bring harm to your body and pain to your stomach.
Eating meat is not good, and drinking wine is not good; rather, you should offer these things to those who are weak.
A bold virgin will not be saved, and one living luxuriously will not see her bridegroom.
Do not say, "The servant girl has grieved me, and I will punish her," because there is no slavery among the daughters of God.
Do not give your ear to vain words, and flee the tales of old women who go about.
Do not look upon the feasts of drunkards, and do not enter the weddings of strangers. For every virgin who does these things is unclean before the Lord.
Open your mouth with the word of God, and restrain your tongue from much speaking.
Humble yourself before the Lord, and his right hand will exalt you.
Do not turn away from the poor in time of affliction, and oil will not be lacking in your lamp.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Evagrius begins his exhortation with a series of short counsels addressed directly to the virgin, urging love of Christ, honor for her mother and sisters, constant prayer, and avoidance of men, anger, luxury, and worldly distractions.
